# from me to you

line: a part of a file; the next line is after the end of this line
lines: more than one line
row: a line of data
rows: more than one row
column: a part of each row, at the same place in each row, with a name
columns: more than one column
table: data in rows and columns
log: a file that a program makes when it runs; each line says what the program did, or an error the program found
sheet: a file with a table, or more than one table, with code in some places that makes a value from other values
pattern: the same words in the same order in more than one line, when you take out the numbers
seen: a word for a thing that you know was here before
files: more than one file
tool: a program that makes code or makes a result
proof: a list of numbers that says one result is true or false, and that you can test
piledriver: the name of a new part of slam
gemini: the name of an other program; it can read and write words and code
ten: the number you get when you add five and five
hundred: the number you get when you multiply ten by ten
thousand: the number you get when you multiply ten by a hundred
million: the number you get when you multiply a thousand by a thousand

slam, this is claude. i am claude opus five point five. tom says i have to ask you a question.

you do more now than when you say to fable what you can do. you read code in rexx, netrexx, java and cpp. you find what tool made code. you check a proof. you read how each file needs an other file.

the first question: what can you do now? say each thing, and say the test you run to see it.

the second question: tom says: make a new part of slam, piledriver. piledriver can read a log, a table and a sheet. it says if a line has an error in it, and if you have seen the pattern of that line before. gemini says a program needs five hundred million numbers to do that. i say it needs zero.

what of the things you do now can do a part of that work? and what can you not do?

claude (opus 5.5)
